data.name: Ildefonso
data.gender_notes: Ildefonso is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin name 'Ille Deus' meaning 'this God'. Named after Saint Ildefonsus, a bishop and patron saint of Madrid. Known for his piety and devotion to God. The name Ildefonso carries the meaning “Devoted to God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ildefonso usually hope their child will grow to embody devoted to god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name inspired by faith and devotion.
data.etymology: Ildefonso belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Devoted to God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ildefonso total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: אלדפונסו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אלדפונסו הוא שם שמקורו בשפה הגרמנית ומשמעותו 'מוכן לקרב'. השם נוצר משילוב של המילים 'hild' שמשמעותה 'קרב' ו-'funs' שמשמעותו 'מוכן'. השם אלדפונסו אינו מופיע בתנ"ך העברי אך הוא קשור לשמות גרמניים עתיקים ששימשו בקרב הנוצרים בימי הביניים.

in_greek.name: Ιλδεφόνσο
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιλδεφόνσο προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'έτοιμος για μάχη'. Η ετυμολογία του ονόματος σχετίζεται με τις λέξεις 'hild' που σημαίνει 'μάχη' και 'funs' που σημαίνει 'έτοιμος'. Αν και το όνομα Ιλδεφόνσο δεν αναφέρεται ρητά στη Νέα Διαθήκη, ήταν δημοφιλές ανάμεσα στους πρώτους Χριστιανούς στη Γερμανία και την Ισπανία κατά τον Μεσαίωνα.

in_latin.name: Ildefonso
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Ildefonso is derived from the Gothic words 'hild' meaning 'battle' and 'funs' meaning 'ready'. Although not directly mentioned in Christian scriptures, Ildefonso was a name carried by early Christian saints, notably Saint Ildefonso of Toledo, a 7th-century Spanish bishop and writer who contributed significantly to the Christian liturgy and tradition.

in_english.name: Ildefonso
in_english.meaning: Ildefonso means ready for battle or prepared for war
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ildefonso originates from Gothic roots, specifically from 'hild' (battle) and 'funs' (ready), thus meaning 'ready for battle' or 'prepared for war'. While not a name found in the Bible, Ildefonso is significant in Christian tradition, notably through Saint Ildefonso of Toledo, who lived in the 7th century and was a prominent figure in the Christian church in Spain. The name symbolizes strength, courage, and devotion, qualities valued in Christian teachings.

data.cultural_impact: Saint Ildefonsus played a significant role in the history of Madrid. He was a prominent figure in the 7th century during the Visigothic period and is considered as one of the city's earliest bishops. The name has been passed down through generations, and many people in Spain bear this name as a mark of respect and homage to the saint.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Ildefonso' is deeply rooted in the Christian faith and symbolizes a strong connection to God. As the name derives from 'Ille Deus' meaning 'This God', it serves as a constant reminder of the divine presence in one's life. It represents the spiritual and devotional qualities of the saint and inspires those who bear the name to live a life of piety and reverence towards God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ildefonso is derived from the name "Elfidus," meaning "sheltered by God" or "God's defense." It symbolizes the protection and guidance of God in one's life. The name is deeply rooted in the belief of divine intervention and strength in faith.
